duplicate_groups.reason: These are distinct reports of a shared causal defect, not literal copies: the Pylint 2.5 pragma tokenizer used an overly restrictive MESSAGE_STRING character class for previously accepted symbolic disable targets. The initial class [A-Za-z\-]{2,} excluded both underscores and digits. The first repair adds underscores; the second repair directly modifies that resulting class to add digits. Thus underscore-containing and digit-containing names trigger different manifestations of the same incomplete identifier-token definition. Grouping is supported by the concrete shared tokenizer rule and successive repairs, rather than merely by similar symptoms or related features.

reviews.mechanism: The pragma parser's MESSAGE_STRING character class excluded underscores, splitting the plugin message name found-_-in-module-class into invalid fragments instead of recognizing a complete disable target.
reviews.reason: The report identifies a regression from Pylint 2.4.4 to 2.5.0: the symbolic name produces bad-option-value errors and fails to suppress the warning, whereas W9902 works. The implementation adds underscores to MESSAGE_STRING. Despite the changelog and test naming referring to dashes, the regression assertion uses raw_input-builtin, which concretely exercises an underscore.

reviews.mechanism: The pragma parser's MESSAGE_STRING character class excluded digits, preventing a checker name such as j3-no-jfly from being recognized as a complete disable target.
reviews.reason: The report traces the 2.4.4-to-2.5.0 regression to the MESSAGE_STRING regex and describes an error reporting only the suffix -no-jfly. The implementation adds digits to the character class, and the regression assertion requires j3-custom-checker to remain a single parsed message name.
